translations.literal: When the Zhou Ancestor entered the capital the hundred officials paid court; seeing Dao he still performed a bow, expecting Dao to proceed with acclamation; Dao received the bow as in ordinary times and said slowly: "This journey of the Palace Attendant is not easy."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu entered the capital the officials paid court; seeing Feng Dao he bowed, expecting acclamation; Dao received the bow as usual and said slowly: "This journey of yours, Palace Attendant, is not easy."

sentences.zh: 」周祖氣沮，故禪代之謀稍緩。

translations.literal: " The Zhou Ancestor's spirit was deflated, and therefore the plan for abdication and succession slowed.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu's spirits sank, and his plan to seize the throne slowed.

sentences.zh: 及請道詣徐州冊湘陰公為漢嗣，道曰：「侍中由衷乎？

translations.literal: When he asked Dao to go to Xuzhou to invest the Duke of Xiangyin as heir of Han, Dao said: "Is the Palace Attendant sincere from the heart?"
translations.idiomatic: When he asked Dao to go to Xuzhou to invest the Duke of Xiangyin as Han heir, Dao said: "Are you sincere, Palace Attendant?"

sentences.zh: 」周祖設誓，道曰：「莫教老夫為謬語，令為謬語人。

translations.literal: " The Zhou Ancestor swore an oath; Dao said: "Do not make this old man speak false words and become a man of false words."
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu swore an oath; Dao said: "Do not make me speak falsehood and become a liar."

sentences.zh: 」臣謹案，周世宗朝，詔御史臣修《周祖實錄》，故道之事，所宜諱矣。）〉

translations.literal: " Your subject respectfully notes that in the reign of Shizong of Zhou an edict ordered this censor to compile the 《Veritable Records of the Zhou Ancestor》; matters concerning Dao were therefore properly to be omitted.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " This compiler notes that in Shizong's reign an edict ordered the compilation of the 《Veritable Records of Zhou Taizu》; matters concerning Dao were therefore properly omitted.)〉

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：周太祖昔在初潛，未聞多譽，洎西平蒲阪，北鎮鄴臺，有統御之勞，顯英偉之量。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In his early obscurity the Zhou Grand Ancestor was not much praised; when he pacified the west at Puban and held the north at Ye Terrace he showed merit in command and the measure of a hero.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In early obscurity Zhou Taizu won little praise; after pacifying Puban in the west and holding Ye in the north he showed commander's merit and heroic stature.

sentences.zh: 旋屬漢道斯季，天命有歸。

translations.literal: Soon the Han way reached its season's end and Heaven's mandate had a destination.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Han way reached its end and Heaven's mandate found its heir.

sentences.zh: 總虎旅以蕩神京，不無慚德；

translations.literal: He gathered tiger brigades to shake the divine capital—not without shame in virtue;
translations.idiomatic: He gathered armies to shake the divine capital—not without moral shame;

sentences.zh: 攬龍圖而登帝位，遂闡皇風。

translations.literal: he embraced the dragon chart and ascended the imperial throne, and thereupon unfolded imperial style.
translations.idiomatic: yet he embraced the dragon chart, took the throne, and unfolded imperial rule.

sentences.zh: 期月而弊政皆除，逾歲而群情大服，何遷善之如是，蓋應變以無窮者也。

translations.literal: Within a month corrupt policies were all removed; within a year popular sentiment was greatly won—how swift his turning to the good; it was because he adapted to change without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month corrupt policies were gone; within a year the people were won—how swiftly he turned to good governance, adapting without limit to every change.

sentences.zh: 所以魯國兇徒，望風而散，並門遺孽，引日偷生。

translations.literal: Therefore the vicious bands of Lu dispersed at the wind of his approach; the remnant evils of Bingmen dragged out their days in stealth.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the vicious bands of Lu scattered at his approach, while Bingmen's remnant rebels dragged out their days in hiding.

sentences.zh: 及鼎駕之將升，命瓦棺而薄葬，勤儉之美，終始可稱。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to ascend he ordered a pottery coffin and plain burial; the beauty of diligence and frugality was admirable from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached he ordered a pottery coffin and plain burial; his diligence and frugality were admirable to the end.

sentences.zh: 雖享國之非長，亦開基之有裕矣。

translations.literal: Though his possession of the realm was not long, yet in founding the dynasty he was ample.
translations.idiomatic: Though his reign was brief, he laid a foundation with room to grow.

sentences.zh: 然而二王之誅，議者譏其不能駕馭權豪，傷於猜忍，卜年斯促，抑有由焉。

translations.literal: Yet the executions of the two kings—commentators criticized his inability to control powerful magnates, his injury from suspicion and harshness; that his allotted years were so brief also had its reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the executions of the two kings drew criticism that he could not control powerful magnates and was wounded by suspicion and harshness; that his reign was brief also had its causes.
